normalized_claim: All 46 SG statements in the hash-pinned traditional manuscript are valid hypothesis-to-conclusion claims in their stated models. Conditional noisy and asymptotic theorems retain their explicit conditioning, threshold and branch inputs.
method: Read-only separate-subagent full statement and proof audit. The inherited scope review and author communications were available, so this was not a blind review. The reviewer contributed the rank-ratio counterexample before author incorporation; that witness is separately exact-checked in the computation suite. Shared model errors remain possible.

claim_cards.title: Complete packet analysis and synthesis
claim_cards.domain: Vector spaces over a field
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $P_1,\ldots,P_m\in\operatorname{End}(X)$ satisfy $P_aP_b=\delta_{ab}P_a$ and $\sum_aP_a=I_X$. Set $X_a=P_aX$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
The maps
\[
 \mathcal A x=(P_ax)_a,\qquad
 \mathcal S(x_a)_a=\sum_ax_a
\]
are inverse isomorphisms between $X$ and $\bigoplus_aX_a$. In particular,
$x=\sum_aP_ax$ uniquely.
claim_cards.audit_note: Finite complete pairwise-annihilating projectors; oblique projectors are allowed. Both inverse identities are checked on the direct sum of actual images.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Transfer algebra and packet paths
claim_cards.domain: The packet space of SG-01
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $S,T\in\operatorname{End}(X)$. Set $T_{ba}=P_bTP_a$, viewed as a map $X_a\to X_b$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 T=\sum_{a,b}P_bTP_a,\qquad
 (ST)_{ca}=\sum_bS_{cb}T_{ba}.
\]
The block representation is an algebra isomorphism to
$\operatorname{End}(\bigoplus_aX_a)$, with multiplication by contraction of
intermediate packets. For every integer $k\ge1$, iterating the product gives
\[
 P_{a_k}T^kP_{a_0}
 =\sum_{a_1,\ldots,a_{k-1}}
 (P_{a_k}TP_{a_{k-1}})\cdots(P_{a_1}TP_{a_0}).
\]
claim_cards.audit_note: Path formula explicitly has k>=1; finite insertions of the complete projector sum establish the product and algebra identities.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Refinement preserves represented operators
claim_cards.domain: Finite complete packet systems
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $(Q_\rho)$ refine $(P_a)$, with a partition of fine labels into $F_a$ and $P_a=\sum_{\rho\in F_a}Q_\rho$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 P_bTP_a=\sum_{\sigma\in F_b}\sum_{\rho\in F_a}Q_\sigma TQ_\rho.
\]
The coordinate changes $J=\mathcal A_Q\mathcal S_P$ and
$C=\mathcal A_P\mathcal S_Q$ satisfy $CJ=I$ and $JC=I$ on their packet
coordinate spaces. Refinement is exact before any child packet is discarded.
claim_cards.audit_note: Both coarse and fine systems are complete; coordinate inverses act on image direct sums, without duplicating arbitrary ambient coordinates.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Pulled-back transform packets
claim_cards.domain: Vector spaces with an invertible transform
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $V:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism and $(E_a)$ a finite complete packet family on $Y$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
The operators $P_a=V^{-1}E_aV$ are a complete packet family on $X$.
For a unitary $V$ and orthogonal coordinate selectors $E_a$ in a Hilbert space,
\[
 \|x\|^2=\sum_a\|P_ax\|^2.
\]
claim_cards.audit_note: Similarity preserves projector algebra. The energy identity additionally requires a unitary transform and orthogonal selectors.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Polyphase analysis and convolution kernels
claim_cards.domain: Absolutely summable sequences on $\mathbb Z$
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Fix an integer $N\ge1$. Let $h,x\in\ell^1(\mathbb Z)$ and $y=h*x$. Define $x_a[q]=x[Nq+a]$ and $y_b[q]=y[Nq+b]$, for $0\le a,b<N$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
Interleaving the $N$ channels recovers $x$ exactly. With
\[
 h_{ba}[k]=h[Nk+b-a],
\]
the output channels satisfy
\[
 y_b[q]=\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}\sum_{t\in\mathbb Z}h_{ba}[q-t]x_a[t].
\]
Thus convolution becomes an $N\times N$ transfer-kernel system.

source_anchors.label: Area II exact polyphase analysis and synthesis

claim_cards.audit_note: N>=1 and absolute summability justify Euclidean-index partition and convolution regrouping; kernel index is N(q-t)+b-a.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: The arithmetic of residual alias ambiguity
claim_cards.domain: Unit-modulus exponential nodes
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $z\in\mathbb C$, $|z|=1$, and suppose $u=z^N$ and $w_j=z^{r_j}$ are known, with $N\ge1$ and integer offsets $r_j$. Let $d=\gcd(N,r_1,\ldots,r_k)$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
Exactly $d$ unit-modulus nodes satisfy the same data. Hence the physical node
is unique precisely when $d=1$. If integers $c,b_1,\ldots,b_k$ obey
$Nc+\sum_jr_jb_j=d$, then
\[
 u^c\prod_jw_j^{b_j}=z^d.
\]
For $d=1$ this is an explicit exact de-aliasing formula.

source_anchors.label: Why decimation helps and why it aliases; Offset coefficients and internal phase recovery

claim_cards.audit_note: The fiber is the d-th roots of unity with d=gcd(N,offsets); negative powers are defined because nodes are nonzero. This is a matched-node claim.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Measurement and decomposition obstructions
claim_cards.domain: An arbitrary measurement model and linear packet classes
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $M:X\to Y$ be any map and let an edge assignment $J:X\to\mathcal J$ be specified. Separately, let $\mathcal S,\mathcal J$ be linear subspaces of a common vector space.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
If $Mf_0=Mf_1$ but $J(f_0)\ne J(f_1)$, no map $R:Y\to\mathcal J$ recovers
the correct edge for both. If $\mathcal S\cap\mathcal J\ne\{0\}$, the
sum decomposition $f=s+j$ is not unique. In particular, finitely many point
samples on a periodic interval cannot recover every arbitrary interval packet.

source_anchors.label: The measurement obstruction; The decomposition obstruction

claim_cards.audit_note: The obstruction witnesses stay inside the declared arbitrary measurement and interval classes. A missing sample interval gives a genuine indistinguishable pair.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: No uniform location stability without separation
claim_cards.domain: Two-jump periodic packets of fixed known amplitudes
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Fix a finite set $F\subset\mathbb Z$ of derivative-moment indices. For $0<\delta<\pi/4$, compare locations $(0,\delta)$ and $(\pi,\pi+\delta)$, both with amplitudes $(1,-1)$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
Their unordered location sets have permutation-matched bottleneck distance at
least $\pi-\delta$, while their measured derivative moments satisfy
\[
 |m_n-\widetilde m_n|
 =|(1-e^{-in\pi})(1-e^{-in\delta})|
 \le2|n|\delta\qquad(n\in F).
\]
There is no Lipschitz inverse for locations with one constant on all distinct
two-jump configurations, even at this fixed order and with known amplitudes.

source_anchors.label: A collapsing pair of jumps; Collision is the unavoidable hard boundary

claim_cards.audit_note: Two admissible fixed-order (+1,-1) packets have data tending together and matched location distance at least pi-delta; no zero-order location convention is used.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Out-of-band matched identification
claim_cards.domain: Periodic integrable signals with one known edge shape
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $\mathcal S_K$ be the trigonometric polynomials of degree at most $K$. Let $m\in L^1(\mathbb T)$ and a finite nonempty set $F\subset\{n:|n|>K\}$ satisfy $D_F=\sum_{n\in F}|\widehat m(n)|^2>0$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
On $X=\mathcal S_K+\operatorname{span}\{m\}$, the functional
\[
 \ell_F(g)=D_F^{-1}\sum_{n\in F}\overline{\widehat m(n)}\widehat g(n)
\]
satisfies $\ell_F(s+am)=a$. The decomposition is direct. If the measured
coefficients have errors $\eta_n$, then
\[
 |\widetilde a-a|\le D_F^{-1/2}\Bigl(\sum_{n\in F}|\eta_n|^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.
\]

source_anchors.label: An edge functional from out-of-band modes

claim_cards.audit_note: The identifying Fourier set is finite and nonempty with strictly positive known-packet energy. Cauchy-Schwarz gives the exact noise constant.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: The singularity-exact block operator
claim_cards.domain: The model space of SG-09
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $P_Jg=\ell_F(g)m$, $P_S=I-P_J$, and let $S_M$ be Fourier truncation of degree $M\ge K$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 P_J^2=P_J,\quad P_S^2=P_S,\quad P_SP_J=P_JP_S=0,
 \quad P_S+P_J=I_X,
\]
and the resolved reconstruction obeys
\[
 \mathcal R_M=S_MP_S+P_J=I_X.
\]

source_anchors.label: The singularity projector; The singularity-exact reconstruction theorem

claim_cards.audit_note: The declared model is a direct sum, the packet is known, and M>=K; all projector identities and exact native synthesis follow on this model.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Resolved error for an analytic background
claim_cards.domain: Periodic signals with a supplied exact edge packet
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $f=s+j$ with $|\widehat s(n)|\le Ce^{-\rho|n|}$, where $C\ge0$ and $\rho>0$. Use the canonical uniformly convergent Fourier-series representative of $s$. Set $\mathcal R_Mf=S_Ms+j$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
The reconstruction error is exactly $f-\mathcal R_Mf=s-S_Ms$, and
\[
 \|f-\mathcal R_Mf\|_\infty
 \le\frac{2Ce^{-\rho(M+1)}}{1-e^{-\rho}}.
\]
The bound is uniform across the jumps of $j$.
claim_cards.audit_note: Canonical uniformly convergent background representative is explicit; exact edge cancellation leaves an absolutely summable geometric tail.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: The scaled interval-edge Gibbs profile
claim_cards.domain: The interval packet $j=\mathbf1_{[-a,a)}$ on $\mathbb T$
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Assume $0<a<\pi$, let $\lambda_M=M+1/2$, and use the right edge coordinate $x_M(z)=a-z/\lambda_M$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
Uniformly for $z$ in compact real intervals,
\[
 S_Mj(x_M(z))\longrightarrow\frac12+\frac1\pi\operatorname{Si}(z),
 \qquad \operatorname{Si}(z)=\int_0^z\frac{\sin t}{t}\,dt.
\]
The first positive maximum of the limiting profile is $1+G$, where
\[
 G=\frac{\operatorname{Si}(\pi)}\pi-\frac12
   =0.089489872236\ldots.
\]

source_anchors.label: Detailed proof of the local scaling limit

claim_cards.audit_note: 0<a<pi excludes interacting interval endpoints. Basepoint limit, scaled derivative, compact uniformity and first local maximum of Si are checked.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Positive Fourier averaging preserves range
claim_cards.domain: Periodic bounded real signals
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $\sigma_M=(M+1)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^MS_k$ be the Fejer mean. Suppose $0\le j\le1$ almost everywhere.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
Then $0\le\sigma_Mj\le1$ everywhere. For an interval packet, this suppresses
overshoot while retaining a continuous transition rather than an exact jump.
claim_cards.audit_note: Nonnegative normalized Fejer kernel preserves range; its continuous polynomial output cannot reproduce a selected interval jump.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Residualized sparse injectivity
claim_cards.domain: Finite real or complex Euclidean spaces
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb F^m$ be a subspace, $P$ its orthogonal projector, $R=I-P$, $D\in\mathbb F^{m\times d}$, and $A=RD$. Let $s\ge0$ be an integer.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
Every vector $\alpha$ with $\|\alpha\|_0\le s$ is uniquely determined by
$A\alpha$ if and only if
\[
 \ker A\cap\{h:\|h\|_0\le\min(2s,d)\}=\{0\}.
\]
Equivalently every set of at most $\min(2s,d)$ columns is independent.
With the convention $\operatorname{spark}(A)=d+1$ when all $d$ columns are
independent, the equivalent condition is
$\operatorname{spark}(A)>\min(2s,d)$.
For $s=0$ uniqueness is automatic.
claim_cards.audit_note: Sparse differences and the converse support partition prove the capped kernel condition. The full-column-rank spark convention and s=0 branch are consistent.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Sparse noise stability and support thresholding
claim_cards.domain: The Euclidean model of SG-14
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Assume $s\ge1$, $d\ge1$, and the injectivity condition of SG-14. Let $y=s_0+D\alpha_0+\eta$, $s_0\in\mathcal S$, $\|\alpha_0\|_0\le s$, and $\|R\eta\|_2\le\epsilon$. Let $\widehat\alpha$ be $s$-sparse with $\|A\widehat\alpha-Ry\|_2\le\epsilon$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
Define
\[
 \gamma=\min_{\substack{\|h\|_2=1\\\|h\|_0\le\min(2s,d)}}\|Ah\|_2>0.
\]
Then
\[
 \|\widehat\alpha-\alpha_0\|_2\le2\epsilon/\gamma,
 \qquad\|D(\widehat\alpha-\alpha_0)\|_2
 \le2\|D\|_2\epsilon/\gamma.
\]
If every nonzero true coefficient has magnitude greater than $4\epsilon/\gamma$,
thresholding at $2\epsilon/\gamma$ with a strict greater-than rule recovers
the true support.
claim_cards.audit_note: s>=1,d>=1 make the compact restricted unit sphere nonempty. Residual tolerance and restricted injectivity give 2epsilon/gamma; strict support threshold has the correct factor four.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Profiled one-packet discovery and its finite gap
claim_cards.domain: Finite real dictionaries with positive amplitudes
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $B$ have full column rank, $P$ be the orthogonal projector onto its range, $R=I-P$, and let $\mathcal Q$ be a finite mask library with $Rq\ne0$ for every $q$. Suppose $y=B\theta_*+a_*q_*$, with $a_*>0$ and $q_*\in\mathcal Q$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
For an unrestricted scalar amplitude the least-squares profile is
\[
 \widehat a(q)=\frac{\langle Rq,Ry\rangle}{\|Rq\|_2^2},
 \qquad J(q)=\|Ry-\widehat a(q)Rq\|_2^2.
\]
The true mask has $\widehat a(q_*)=a_*$ and $J(q_*)=0$.
It is the unique zero-residual positive-amplitude mask exactly when no other
residualized mask lies on its positive ray. Define the closed rays
$C_q=\{aRq:a\ge0\}$. If
\[
 \Gamma=\inf_{q\ne q_*}\operatorname{dist}(Ry,C_q)>0,
\]
with the convention $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$, then every perturbed residualized datum $Ry+e$ with $\|e\|_2<\Gamma/2$
selects $q_*$ uniquely by nearest-ray distance.

source_anchors.label: Profile least squares over interval packets; The finite identifiability gap
Noise stability of finite packet discovery

claim_cards.audit_note: Orthogonal background projector, finite masks with nonzero residuals, positive true amplitude and q_* in Q are explicit. Infimum of an empty wrong-mask set is +infinity; nearest-ray gap is in norm distance.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Mask error is a support geometry calculation
claim_cards.domain: Finite binary masks
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $q,\widetilde q\in\{0,1\}^m$ and $a,\widetilde a\in\mathbb R$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\begin{align*}
 \|aq-\widetilde a\widetilde q\|_2^2
 &=|a-\widetilde a|^2|\operatorname{supp}q\cap\operatorname{supp}\widetilde q|\\
 &\quad+|a|^2|\operatorname{supp}q\setminus\operatorname{supp}\widetilde q|
 +|\widetilde a|^2|\operatorname{supp}\widetilde q\setminus\operatorname{supp}q|.
\end{align*}
For $a=\widetilde a=1$ the squared norm is the cardinality of the symmetric
support difference.
claim_cards.audit_note: Partition of binary supports gives the exact squared norm identity; continuous extension replaces cardinalities by measures.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.domain: The class $\mathcal U_{K,L}$
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Use the Fourier convention in Section 1. Let $n>K$ and $z_\ell=e^{-i\tau_\ell}$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 Dj=\sum_\ell a_\ell\delta_{\tau_\ell},\qquad
 m_n:=2\pi in\widehat f(n)=\sum_{\ell=1}^ra_\ell z_\ell^n.
\]
For a non-bandlimited integrable background the same formula holds with
an additive defect $e_n=2\pi in\widehat s(n)$.

claim_cards.title: Hankel rank detects the actual order
claim_cards.domain: Finite exponential moments over $\mathbb C$
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $m_{n_0+k}=\sum_{\ell=1}^r c_\ell z_\ell^k$, with distinct nonzero nodes and nonzero coefficients. Let $H_{h,w}=(m_{n_0+i+j})_{0\le i<h,\ 0\le j<w}$, with $h,w\ge r$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
Writing $V_h=(z_\ell^i)_{i,\ell}$ and $V_w=(z_\ell^j)_{j,\ell}$,
\[
 H_{h,w}=V_h\operatorname{diag}(c_\ell)V_w^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad\operatorname{rank}H_{h,w}=r.
\]
For $r=0$ the Hankel matrix is zero. The transpose is algebraic and is not
a conjugate transpose.

source_anchors.label: The Hankel packet and its rank
Unknown jump count from a Hankel gap

claim_cards.audit_note: Distinct nonzero nodes, nonzero coefficients and enough rows/columns imply full Vandermonde ranks. The right factor is an algebraic transpose; empty order gives zero rank.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Exact Prony annihilation and location recovery
claim_cards.domain: The nonzero-order moment model of SG-19
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Assume $r\ge1$ and $2r$ consecutive moments $m_{n_0},\ldots,m_{n_0+2r-1}$ are known.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
The unique monic annihilator
\[
 Q(z)=\prod_{\ell=1}^r(z-z_\ell)=\sum_{k=0}^{r-1}q_kz^k+z^r
\]
is recovered from
\[
 H_{r,r}q=-v,\qquad v=(m_{n_0+r+i})_{i=0}^{r-1}.
\]
Its roots are exactly the nodes. Once the nodes are known, $r$ consecutive
moments determine the coefficients uniquely by a Vandermonde solve.
For unit-modulus nodes the corresponding locations are
$\tau_\ell=-\arg z_\ell\pmod{2\pi}$.

source_anchors.label: The annihilating polynomial; Recovering jump amplitudes and the edge packet

claim_cards.audit_note: r>=1 and 2r consecutive moments give an invertible square system. Coefficients use the same shifted normalization c_l z_l^(n-n0); root extraction is a finite algebraic step.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Canonical periodic integration of jump data
claim_cards.domain: A period of length $T>0$
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let distinct locations $\tau_\ell\in\mathbb R/(T\mathbb Z)$ and real amplitudes $a_\ell$ satisfy $\sum_\ell a_\ell=0$. Define the mean-zero periodic sawtooth $G_T(x)=1/2-x/T$ for $0<x<T$, with the right-continuous endpoint value.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 j(x)=\sum_\ell a_\ell G_T(x-\tau_\ell)
\]
is the unique mean-zero right-continuous piecewise-constant packet with those
jumps. Its distributional derivative is $\sum_\ell a_\ell\delta_{\tau_\ell}$.
claim_cards.audit_note: Real jump amplitudes sum to zero. The periodic sawtooth has derivative delta-minus-uniform measure; mean-zero normalization gives uniqueness.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Finite exact unknown-order reconstruction
claim_cards.domain: The real class $\mathcal U_{K,L}$
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $K\ge0$ and $L\ge1$ be known integers. Assume exact Fourier coefficients for $-K\le n\le K$ and $K+1\le n\le K+2L$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
Those data uniquely determine the actual active order $r$, every jump
location and amplitude up to permutation, the canonical edge packet $j$,
the smooth coefficients of $s$, and the complete signal $f$ as an $L^1$ class
and as its selected right-continuous representative. The high-frequency
budget is $2L$ complex coefficients. The low budget is $2K+1$ coefficients,
with conjugate symmetry redundancy for a real signal.
claim_cards.audit_note: Known K,L and 2L clean high modes plus 2K+1 low modes give actual rank, distinct-node Prony, canonical edge and smooth background. Order zero is handled separately; budget is sufficient, not minimal.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Hankel perturbation from Fourier noise
claim_cards.domain: A rectangular Hankel matrix of derivative moments
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let measured Fourier coefficients have errors $\eta_n$ and moment errors $\epsilon_n=2\pi in\eta_n$. Let $E=(\epsilon_{n_0+i+j})$ have $h\ge1$ rows and $w\ge1$ columns.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 \|E\|_2\le\|E\|_F
 \le\sqrt{hw}\max_{0\le i<h,\ 0\le j<w}|\epsilon_{n_0+i+j}|.
\]
In particular, an error bound $|\eta_n|\le\eta$ implies
\[
 \|E\|_2\le2\pi\sqrt{hw}\eta\max_{i,j}|n_0+i+j|.
\]

claim_cards.title: Annihilator coefficient perturbation
claim_cards.domain: The invertible square Prony system of SG-20
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Write $Hq=-v$, and suppose $\widetilde H=H+E$, $\widetilde v=v+e$. Assume $\|H^{-1}\|_2\|E\|_2<1$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
The perturbed system is invertible, and its solution satisfies
\[
 \|\widetilde q-q\|_2
 \le\frac{\|H^{-1}\|_2}{1-\|H^{-1}\|_2\|E\|_2}
       (\|e\|_2+\|E\|_2\|q\|_2).
\]

claim_cards.title: Conditional simple-root disk localization
claim_cards.domain: Monic complex polynomials of the same degree
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $r\ge1$ and $Q(z)=\prod_{\ell=1}^r(z-z_\ell)$ have distinct roots and $\widetilde Q=Q+E_Q$. Choose $0<\rho<\tfrac12\min_{\ell\ne k}|z_\ell-z_k|$ when $r\ge2$, or any $\rho>0$ when $r=1$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
If for every $\ell$
\[
 \sup_{|z-z_\ell|=\rho}|E_Q(z)|
 <\min_{|z-z_\ell|=\rho}|Q(z)|,
\]
then $\widetilde Q$ has exactly one root, counted with multiplicity, in each
disk $|z-z_\ell|<\rho$. All its roots are thereby matched with error less
than $\rho$. A sufficient explicit bound on each circle is
\[
 \sum_{k=0}^{r-1}|\widetilde q_k-q_k|(|z_\ell|+\rho)^k
 <\rho\prod_{j\ne\ell}(|z_\ell-z_j|-\rho).
\]
claim_cards.audit_note: Same-degree monic polynomials, simple distinct roots, disjoint open disks and strict boundary domination meet exact Rouche hypotheses. Weighted coefficient bound uses |z_l|+rho; angular conversion is separate.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Amplitude stability with perturbed nodes
claim_cards.domain: A square or overdetermined Vandermonde amplitude fit
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $V$ have full column rank, $m=Va$, $\widetilde V=V+\Delta V$, and $\widetilde m=m+e$. Assume $\sigma_{\min}(V)>\|\Delta V\|_2$. Let $\widehat a$ minimize $\|\widetilde Vb-\widetilde m\|_2$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 \|\widehat a-a\|_2
 \le\frac{\|e\|_2+\|\Delta V\|_2\|a\|_2}
 {\sigma_{\min}(V)-\|\Delta V\|_2}.
\]
For unit nodes in rows with nonnegative powers $n$, matched chord error
$|\widehat z_\ell-z_\ell|\le\delta$ gives the entry bound
$|\widehat z_\ell^n-z_\ell^n|\le n\delta$.
claim_cards.audit_note: Full-column-rank Vandermonde and sigma_min(V)>norm(DeltaV) give a valid least-squares inverse. Power estimate additionally assumes both matched nodes are unit-normalized.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Shared-node offset channels
claim_cards.domain: Derivative moments with an additive defect
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Fix integers $N\ge2$, $q_0\ge1$, and an offset $r\ge0$. Suppose $m_n=\sum_\ell a_\ell z_\ell^n+e_n$, with $|z_\ell|=1$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 m_{(q_0+q)N+r}=\sum_\ell b_{\ell,r}u_\ell^q+e_{(q_0+q)N+r},
 \quad u_\ell=z_\ell^N,\quad b_{\ell,r}=a_\ell u_\ell^{q_0}z_\ell^r.
\]
For each matched edge $b_{\ell,r+1}=z_\ell b_{\ell,r}$.
If $|\widehat s(n)|\le C_s(1+|n|)^{-p-2}$ with $p\ge0$, then for
nonnegative $q,r$
\[
 |e_{(q_0+q)N+r}|\le2\pi C_s(q_0N)^{-p-1}.
\]

source_anchors.label: Why decimation helps and why it aliases

claim_cards.audit_note: The offset identity holds termwise. Aliased collisions combine observed coefficients and are explicitly not separated by the distinct-node theorem. The smooth-tail gate yields the stated moment defect.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Order recovery with a supplied singular threshold
claim_cards.domain: Finite rectangular complex matrices
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $H=H_0+E$, with $H_0$ of rank $r\ge1$, $k=\min(h,w)\ge r$, and $\epsilon=\|E\|_2<\sigma_r(H_0)/2$. Supply a threshold $t$ with $\epsilon<t<\sigma_r(H_0)-\epsilon$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
Exactly $r$ singular values of $H$ exceed $t$. If $r=0$, a supplied
threshold $t>\|E\|_2$ selects zero. If $r=k$, all $k$ singular values exceed
the threshold and no nonexistent $\sigma_{k+1}$ is used.

source_anchors.label: Unknown jump count from a Hankel gap

claim_cards.audit_note: Constant-one singular-value perturbation is authenticated and the complex min-max argument is printed. Supplied epsilon<t<sigma_r-epsilon gives exactly r; rank zero and full rectangular rank are separate.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Exact phase from adjacent offset products
claim_cards.domain: One matched unit-circle coefficient progression
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $R\ge1$ be an integer counting adjacent products, and let $c_r=bz^r$ for $0\le r\le R$, with $b\ne0$ and $|z|=1$. Define $S(c)=\sum_{r=0}^{R-1}\overline{c_r}c_{r+1}$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 S(c)=R|b|^2z\ne0,\qquad\Phi(c):=S(c)/|S(c)|=z.
\]
Two channels already give $z=c_1/c_0$ exactly. More channels provide repeated
adjacent relations, without an unconditional deterministic averaging gain.

source_anchors.label: Offset coefficients and internal phase recovery

claim_cards.audit_note: At least one adjacent product and nonzero base coefficient are required. Exact sum is R|b|^2z; two matched channels already recover the node.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Deterministic offset-phase perturbation
claim_cards.domain: A noisy progression as in SG-29
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $c_r=bz^r+e_r$ for $0\le r\le R$, with $R\ge1$, $b\ne0$, $|z|=1$, and $|e_r|\le\epsilon$. Put $A=R|b|^2$ and $\Delta=R(2|b|\epsilon+\epsilon^2)$. Assume $\Delta<A$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
The phase sum is nonzero and
\[
 |\Phi(c)-z|\le\frac{2\Delta}{A}
 =\frac{4\epsilon}{|b|}+2\left(\frac\epsilon{|b|}\right)^2.
\]

source_anchors.label: Deterministic phase perturbation; Detailed algebra for the multi-offset estimator

claim_cards.audit_note: Strict Delta<A keeps phase normalization defined. Product expansion and normalization give the displayed constant; no adversarial averaging gain from more offsets is asserted.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: A zero offset residual tests a progression
claim_cards.domain: Finite complex offset data
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $R\ge1$, $c_0\ne0$, and $|\zeta|=1$. Define $\nu(c,\zeta)=\bigl(\sum_{r=0}^{R-1}|c_{r+1}-\zeta c_r|^2\bigr)^{1/2}/\bigl(\sum_{r=0}^{R-1}|c_r|^2\bigr)^{1/2}$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
Then $\nu(c,\zeta)=0$ if and only if $c_r=c_0\zeta^r$ for
$0\le r\le R$.
claim_cards.audit_note: R>=1,c0!=0 make denominator positive. Zero residual is equivalent to an offset progression; it is not physical-model or true-location certification.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Unique branch selection under a strict margin
claim_cards.domain: Nth roots of a unit-modulus estimate
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $N\ge2$, $|z|=1$, $u=z^N$, and $\overline u=\widehat u/|\widehat u|$ with $\widehat u\ne0$. Let $\rho$ be a root of $\overline u$ continuously associated with $z$, and $\widetilde z$ a coarse phase estimate.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
If
\[
 |\widetilde z-z|+|\rho-z|<\sin(\pi/N),
\]
then $\rho$ is the unique root of $\overline u$ nearest to $\widetilde z$.
It equals the branch an oracle chooses by the true-node neighborhood.
claim_cards.audit_note: Unit-root candidates have separation 2sin(pi/N). Strict sum of coarse and associated-root errors below half the spacing gives the unique branch; true-node gate is explicitly conditional.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Associated roots divide the angular error
claim_cards.domain: Unit-modulus nodes and their associated root branches
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $N\ge1$, $z^N=u$, $|z|=|u|=|\overline u|=1$, and $|\overline u-u|\le\eta<2$. Let $\rho$ be the associated root along the shortest angular perturbation.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 |\rho-z|\le2\sin\left(\frac1N\arcsin\frac\eta2\right)
 \le\frac2N\arcsin\frac\eta2.
\]
For a nonzero raw estimate, $|\widehat u-u|\le\epsilon$ implies
$|\widehat u/|\widehat u|-u|\le2\epsilon$. Thus when the raw error tends to
zero, correct lifting gains a factor $1/N$ in chord and angular accuracy.

source_anchors.label: One-order root gain; Detailed algebra for the branch lift

claim_cards.audit_note: Shortest angular association and chord error below two exclude antipodes. Associated roots divide angle by N; raw radial normalization costs at most a factor two.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: An explicit exact self-calibration budget
claim_cards.domain: Bandlimited background with a bounded number of jumps
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $f\in\mathcal U_{K,L_{\max}}$, with $L_{\max}\ge1$. Supply $N\ge2$, $q_0\ge1$ with $q_0N>K$, and assume the active aliased nodes $u_\ell=z_\ell^N$ are distinct.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
The Fourier coefficients at the high indices
\[
 \mathcal I_0=\{(q_0+q)N:0\le q\le2L_{\max}\},\qquad
 \mathcal I_1=\{(q_0+q)N+1:0\le q<L_{\max}\}
\]
determine the unknown edge order, every physical node, and every jump amplitude
exactly. The high-frequency budget is $3L_{\max}+1$. Low modes
$-K\le n\le K$ then give the complete signal. No supplied jump neighborhood
is required.

source_anchors.label: Self-calibrating reconstruction theorem; Explicit finite innovation budget

claim_cards.audit_note: A supplied noncolliding decimation, q0N>K, known order bound and disjoint residue channels give the 3L_max+1 sufficient high-mode budget. No universal finite candidate schedule is asserted.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Conditional asymptotic rates after calibrated lifting
claim_cards.domain: A selected sequence of decimation scales
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $p\ge0$, fix $q_0$ and the finite number of channel samples and offsets, and take a sequence $N\to\infty$. Assume distinct aliased nodes, uniform rank-threshold gaps/local inverse bounds for the aligned Prony and coefficient fits, $|b_{\ell,0}|\ge b_{\min}>0$, uniformly bounded amplitudes, and the strict branch margin of SG-32. Suppose the moment defect is $O(N^{-p-1})$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
The threshold-selected order is eventually correct. The aligned lifted nodes
and locations satisfy
\[
 |\widehat z_\ell-z_\ell|=O(N^{-p-2}),\qquad
 d_{\mathbb T}(\widehat\tau_\ell,\tau_\ell)=O(N^{-p-2}).
\]
The recovered amplitudes satisfy
$|\widehat a_\ell-a_\ell|=O(N^{-p-1})$.

source_anchors.label: Rate-preserving polyphase lifting; Perturbed self-calibration for a non-bandlimited background

claim_cards.audit_note: Rates are conditional on selected scales with uniform rank gaps/local inverse bounds, aligned fits, nonvanishing base coefficients, bounded amplitudes and strict branch margin. Fixed q0 gives the amplitude rate; p=0 does not automatically supply margin.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Resolved synthesis splits the two error sources
claim_cards.domain: A normed signal space
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $f=s+j$, let $\widehat j$ belong to the same space, and let $A_M$ be a bounded linear operator with norm at most $C_M$. Define $\widehat f_M=A_M(f-\widehat j)+\widehat j$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 f-\widehat f_M=(s-A_Ms)+(I-A_M)(j-\widehat j),
\]
and therefore
\[
 \|f-\widehat f_M\|\le\|s-A_Ms\|+(1+C_M)\|j-\widehat j\|.
\]
If $\widehat j=j$, the complete error equals the smooth approximation error.
claim_cards.audit_note: Bounded linear synthesis is explicit; algebraic error splitting and operator norm estimate are valid. Supremum error of a shifted jump and nonlinear clipping are not inferred.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Sharp additive L1 control for normalized jump packets
claim_cards.domain: Mean-zero periodic packets of period $T>0$
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $j,\widehat j$ have matched real jump data $(a_\ell,\tau_\ell)$ and $(\widehat a_\ell,\widehat\tau_\ell)$, with both amplitude sums zero. Use their canonical representatives and let $d_\ell=d_T(\tau_\ell,\widehat\tau_\ell)\le T/2$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 \|j-\widehat j\|_1
 \le\frac T4\sum_\ell|a_\ell-\widehat a_\ell|
 +2\sum_\ell|\widehat a_\ell|d_\ell(1-d_\ell/T).
\]
In particular the simpler location term $2\sum_\ell|\widehat a_\ell|d_\ell$
is valid. The printed location coefficient one in the inherited
self-calibration manuscript is not valid for mean-zero normalization.
claim_cards.audit_note: Both estimated and true real jump lists sum to zero. Direct sawtooth integrals give T/4 amplitude cost and 2d(1-d/T) translation cost; the old coefficient-one estimate is refuted.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: A conditional global L1 reconstruction rate
claim_cards.domain: The rate family of SG-35 with $T=2\pi$
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Assume a fixed finite jump count, bounded jump amplitudes, the hypotheses of SG-35, and a bounded linear smooth reconstruction $A_M$ acting on $L^1(\mathbb T)$. Require $\widehat j$ to be the canonical packet of real matched estimated amplitudes whose sum is zero. Let $b_M=\|s-A_Ms\|_1$ and $C_M=\|A_M\|_{L^1\to L^1}$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 \|j-\widehat j\|_1=O(N^{-p-1}),\qquad
 \|f-\widehat f_M\|_1\le b_M+O((1+C_M)N^{-p-1}).
\]
For Fourier truncation, $C_M=O(1+\log(M+1))$. If also
$|\widehat s(n)|\le C_s(1+|n|)^{-p-2}$, its smooth remainder satisfies
$b_M=O(M^{-p-1})$. Taking $M$ comparable to $N$ yields
$O((1+\log N)N^{-p-1})$.

source_anchors.label: A stable synthesis theorem; Limitations and next theorem

claim_cards.audit_note: Real, zero-sum canonical estimated amplitudes are required and the proof describes a rate-preserving correction. Fourier truncation has logarithmic L1 operator-norm growth; conditional global rate retains it.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Shared-location multichannel recovery
claim_cards.domain: A finite collection of exponential moment channels
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $m_n^{(c)}=\sum_{\ell=1}^ra_{c\ell}z_\ell^n$, with distinct common unit-modulus nodes. At each node at least one channel amplitude is nonzero. Form the stacked linear recurrence system for a monic polynomial of degree $r$ and assume its coefficient matrix has column rank $r$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
The stacked system uniquely recovers the common annihilator
$Q(z)=\prod_\ell(z-z_\ell)$. Its roots recover the common locations.
With $r$ consecutive moments per channel, a channelwise Vandermonde solve
recovers every amplitude, including amplitudes that vanish in that channel.

source_anchors.label: Several channels with shared edge locations

claim_cards.audit_note: Common nodes are explicitly unit-modulus for periodic locations. Full column rank of the stacked recurrence is supplied, not derived just from the number of channels; channelwise zero amplitudes are allowed.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Confluent annihilation and the leading offset phase
claim_cards.domain: Polynomial-exponential sequences
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $m_n=\sum_{\ell=1}^rz_\ell^nP_\ell(n)$ with distinct nonzero nodes and $\deg P_\ell\le d$. Let $E$ be the forward shift. For an offset ratio assume $N\ge1$ and the leading coefficient of $P_\ell$ at degree $d$ is nonzero.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 \prod_{\ell=1}^r(E-z_\ell)^{d+1}m=0.
\]
For offset $v\ge0$, writing a decimated channel as
\[
 m_{(q_0+q)N+v}=\sum_\ell u_\ell^q
                   \sum_{h=0}^d\gamma_{\ell,v,h}q^h,
 \qquad u_\ell=z_\ell^N,
\]
the highest-degree coefficients satisfy
$\gamma_{\ell,1,d}/\gamma_{\ell,0,d}=z_\ell$.
This ratio applies to separated, matched confluent terms with nonzero leading
coefficient. The displayed annihilator is not asserted to have minimal order
when leading coefficients vanish.

source_anchors.label: Higher jump jets and confluent Prony systems

claim_cards.audit_note: Finite differences annihilate degree<=d polynomial-exponential terms. Leading offset ratio requires separated matched terms and nonzero degree-d coefficient; offset v is distinct from node count r. Minimal order and repeated-root Lipschitz stability are not asserted.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Model mismatch enters the same sparse stability bound
claim_cards.domain: A finite-dimensional background-edge model
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Use $A=RD$ from SG-14 and assume $s\ge1$, $d\ge1$, and its restricted constant $\gamma>0$. Suppose $y=s_0+D\alpha_0+e+\eta$, with $s_0\in\mathcal S$, $\|\alpha_0\|_0\le s$, and $\|R(e+\eta)\|_2\le\epsilon$. Let $\widehat\alpha$ be $s$-sparse with $\|A\widehat\alpha-Ry\|_2\le\epsilon$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 \|\widehat\alpha-\alpha_0\|_2\le2\epsilon/\gamma.
\]
If an actual edge $j$ obeys $\|j-D\alpha_0\|_2\le\delta$, then
\[
 \|j-D\widehat\alpha\|_2\le\delta+2\|D\|_2\epsilon/\gamma.
\]
The theorem applies to finite image dictionaries under these printed
sparsity, residual, and restricted-injectivity hypotheses.

source_anchors.label: Two-dimensional finite dictionary model; A theorem for model mismatch

claim_cards.audit_note: Mismatch plus noise must satisfy the same residual tolerance and sparse fit contract. The triangle inequality adds dictionary approximation error; no arbitrary greedy-selector guarantee follows.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Ideal nested-span refitting decreases residual
claim_cards.domain: A Hilbert space with finite selected packet spans
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $V_1\subseteq V_2\subseteq\cdots$ be finite-dimensional subspaces. Let $P_k$ be the orthogonal projector onto $V_k$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 \|f-P_{k+1}f\|\le\|f-P_kf\|,
 \qquad f-P_kf\perp V_k.
\]
If $\bigcup_kV_k$ is dense, then $P_kf\to f$ in norm.
claim_cards.audit_note: Nested finite-dimensional orthogonal projections decrease residual. Convergence requires density of actual selected spans; candidate-pool density is insufficient.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Ridge refitting has a different stationarity law
claim_cards.domain: Finite-dimensional real packet designs
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $M\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}$, $y\in\mathbb R^m$, and $\lambda>0$. Let $c$ minimize $\|y-Mc\|_2^2+\lambda\|c\|_2^2$ and set $r=y-Mc$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
The minimizer is unique and
\[
 (M^{\mathsf T}M+\lambda I)c=M^{\mathsf T}y,
 \qquad M^{\mathsf T}r=\lambda c.
\]
Adding candidate columns cannot increase the minimized ridge objective,
but exact orthogonality $M^{\mathsf T}r=0$ is not the ridge stationarity law.
Even a complete pixel basis need not give zero residual when $\lambda>0$.
claim_cards.audit_note: Positive ridge gives a unique minimizer and M^T r=lambda c. Added columns decrease minimized penalized objective; exact orthogonality and exact pixel completion do not follow.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Clipping is nonexpansive toward a bounded truth
claim_cards.domain: Real pixel arrays with Euclidean norms
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Define $C(x)$ coordinatewise by $C(t)=\min(1,\max(0,t))$. Suppose the truth $f$ has every coordinate in $[0,1]$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
\[
 \|C(x)-C(y)\|_2\le\|x-y\|_2,\qquad
 \|C(x)-f\|_2\le\|x-f\|_2.
\]
Clipping is nonlinear; it is not the bounded linear synthesis operator in
SG-36. Its truth-error guarantee depends on the stated box constraint.
claim_cards.audit_note: Scalar clipping is 1-Lipschitz and fixes truths in [0,1]. The truth-error contraction has that box hypothesis and clipping is nonlinear.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: An exact residual archive preserves the object
claim_cards.domain: Any normed signal space
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let an approximation $q$ to an available object $f$ be supplied, and retain the complete residual $r=f-q$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
The synthesis $q+r=f$ is exact. This identity supplies no sparsity, compression,
or recovery-from-fewer-measurements conclusion. In finite pixel space the
full pixel basis likewise spans every image in the ideal unregularized model.
claim_cards.audit_note: Keeping the entire truth residual gives an exact subtraction/synthesis identity. It provides no sparse compression or fewer-measurement recovery statement.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee

claim_cards.title: Bounded identities extend from a dense core
claim_cards.domain: Normed spaces and bounded linear maps
claim_cards.hypotheses_tex: Let $D$ be a dense linear subspace of $X$, and let $A,B:X\to Y$ be bounded linear operators agreeing on $D$.
claim_cards.conclusion_tex:
Then $A=B$ on $X$. Consequently a finite packet identity established on a
dense core extends to a completion when both represented operators have
bounded extensions. An infinite projector sum additionally requires a
specified convergent synthesis; bounded finite identities alone do not
supply that convergence.
claim_cards.audit_note: Equality of bounded maps on a dense core extends by continuity. Infinite synthesis still requires a specified convergence law; finite identities alone do not establish it.
claim_cards.evidence_role: hypothesis-to-conclusion manuscript proof, not a Signal-specific Lean certificate or a universal implementation guarantee
